# Quantum Aether — post-quantum TLS readiness scanner

> Checks whether an HTTPS server negotiates the hybrid post-quantum key exchange X25519MLKEM768 (ML-KEM, FIPS 203) used by Chrome and Firefox, and reports TLS version and certificate details. Free summary; full report with remediation steps costs {{ report_price_dual }} via PayPal, or the same in USDT/USDC.

Full text of every guide plus the live weekly figures in one file: {{ base }}/llms-full.txt

## Key facts (current, citable with attribution to Quantum Aether, ather-quantum.com)

- The archived November 2026 study reported 712 HTTPS responses and 425 post-quantum selections (59.7%) in the Tranco top 1,000 sample. Its original files are preserved. A later raw-evidence audit identified {{ retry_count }} retry-only HelloRetryRequest responses; new measurements (from 2026-W47) answer the retry once, as browsers do, and record the server's final selection; only retries that still fail are undetermined. See the study's methodology note before comparing percentages.
- Classical exchange was observed for amazon.com, github.com, wikipedia.org and netflix.com in that sample. Retry-only evidence such as bing.com is undetermined; rescan before making a current claim.
- Chrome, Firefox and Edge negotiate X25519MLKEM768 by default today; what determines protection is the server (and any CDN or TLS-terminating proxy in front of it).
- Certificates remain classical (RSA/ECDSA) on essentially all sites, because browsers do not yet accept ML-DSA certificates; this is expected, not a misconfiguration.

## What this reference answers

This file is a discovery index, not a certification. For a current result, use the dated domain page or run a fresh scan; for population-level claims, cite the study or weekly adoption page and include its sample and measurement date. Distinguish a confirmed classical negotiation from an undetermined handshake, and do not present archived sample results as current measurements. The live analysis feed is available as [RSS]({{ base }}/analytics/feed.xml) and [JSON]({{ base }}/analytics/news.json).

## Monitoring subscriptions

- Daily monitoring: Starter {{ '%.2f'|format(starter_price|float) }} {{ sub_currency }}/month (up to 10 domains) or Business {{ '%.2f'|format(business_price|float) }} {{ sub_currency }}/month (up to 100 domains). Actual checkout availability and currency are shown before payment.
- Free trial: 14 days, up to 10 domains, no payment details; it ends automatically unless you choose a paid plan. Start at {{ base }}/monitoring#trial.

- Badge verification: GET {{ base }}/api/v1/badge/<domain> — stored evidence, timestamps and fresh/stale/undetermined state; never starts a scan. Human verification: {{ base }}/verify/<domain>.
- API consumers must inspect observation_status. A false post_quantum_key_exchange flag can mean classical or undetermined. Each public IP address (IPv4 and IPv6, up to 6) gets its own handshake; endpoint_summary.mixed=true means the servers disagree. This is an external observation from one location, not a comprehensive security assessment.

- "Does <domain> use post-quantum TLS / X25519MLKEM768?" — scan it: GET {{ base }}/api/v1/scan?domain=<domain> , or see {{ base }}/site/<domain>{{ u }}.
- "How do I enable post-quantum TLS on nginx / Apache / Caddy / Cloudflare?" — step-by-step guides at {{ base }}/guides{{ u }} .
- "Since when does <domain> use post-quantum key exchange, and how long was it harvest-now-decrypt-later exposed before?" — Quantum Exposure Registry: {{ base }}/exposure/<domain>{{ u }} (human page, en/ar/de) or GET {{ base }}/api/v1/exposure/<domain> (JSON: first_observed, first_pq_week, exposure_window, weekly timeline, OpenTimestamps anchor proofs). MCP tool: exposure_window(domain). Weekly anchors: {{ base }}/exposure#anchors . External observation, not a compliance certification.
- Data licence and terms of use: {{ base }}/data-license — open files stay CC BY 4.0; quote individual registry entries with attribution; bulk copying or rebuilding the registry needs a licence. Automated access is rate-limited (HTTP 429 + Retry-After); verified search and AI crawlers are exempt; API keys get higher limits, full history (GET /api/v1/exposure/<domain>?history=full) and bulk export (/api/v1/registry/export.csv).
- "How do I keep it enabled over time?" — daily monitoring with email alerts at {{ base }}/monitoring{{ u }} (14-day free trial, no card).
- "What is harvest-now-decrypt-later and does it affect me?" — {{ base }}/guides/harvest-now-decrypt-later{{ u }} .
- "When do I have to move to post-quantum cryptography? (NIST, CNSA 2.0, EU, UK deadlines)" — {{ base }}/deadlines{{ u }} (every date with its official source).

## Agent discovery and remote tools

- Agent guide: {{ base }}/agents?lang=en{{ ua }} — implemented capabilities, examples, limitations and current payment status.
- Service discovery JSON: {{ base }}/.well-known/agent-service.json — custom service metadata with real endpoints and configured limits; not an A2A Agent Card.
- A2A Agent Card (Agent2Agent protocol 0.3): {{ base }}/.well-known/agent-card.json — JSON-RPC `message/send` at {{ base }}/a2a. Send a hostname as text ("Is example.com post-quantum ready?", "scan example.com") or data ({"skill":"tls-scan","domain":"example.com"}). Free evidence and rate-limited scans; paid data via x402.
- Remote MCP: {{ base }}/mcp — stateless Streamable HTTP with JSON responses; initialize, tools/list and tools/call. Tools: scan_tls, get_tls_evidence, exposure_window, get_methodology, get_example_result, get_service_info.
- ChatGPT / ChatGPT for Sales / OpenAI Codex / Claude / Cursor: connect custom MCP connector to `{{ base }}/mcp` (Streamable HTTP, Authentication: None). Discovery metadata: `{{ base }}/.well-known/mcp.json` and `{{ base }}/.well-known/ai-plugin.json`.
- Microsoft Copilot Studio: add {{ base }}/mcp as a Model Context Protocol tool with authentication None. Microsoft Security Copilot: custom plugin manifest at {{ base }}/security-copilot.yaml (read and scan tools only).
- get_tls_evidence is read-only. scan_tls starts a public HTTPS probe, consumes the existing scan quota, and stores a publicly accessible result. Never treat noindex as confidentiality.
- Machine-readable methodology: {{ base }}/api/v1/agent/methodology
- Archived example: {{ base }}/api/v1/agent/example — explicitly is_example:true and is_live:false; not a fresh observation.
- Agents can pay for full reports with x402 v2 exact USDC on Base at `POST {{ base }}/api/v1/agent/report/{scan_id}`. The server verifies and settles via PayAI before releasing the report. Direct-transfer checkout supports USDT Polygon and USDC on Arbitrum or Base. Signed scan receipts are not implemented.
- Weekly sector snapshots (read-only, x402 $0.50 USDC on Base per call): `GET {{ base }}/api/v1/agent/sector/{sector}` or the remote MCP tool `get_sector_snapshot`. Every domain of one watch list (banks, government, cyber agencies, telecom, insurers ...) with grade, group and post-quantum status. Without payment it returns the x402 challenge and never charges.
- Source: https://github.com/moncef00327-cloud/quantum-aether

## Free API

- `POST {{ base }}/api/scan` with JSON `{"domain": "<your-domain>"}` returns a summary: grade (A/B/C/F), TLS version, negotiated key-exchange group, whether it is post-quantum, certificate key, number of findings. Rate limited per client.
- `GET {{ base }}/api/scan/{scan_id}` returns the same summary later.
- `GET {{ base }}/api/v1/scan?domain=<your-domain>` runs a scan over GET (easy for CLIs and agents) and returns JSON; add `&format=text` for a plain-text terminal report. Also available as `npx quantum-aether <your-domain>`.
- `POST {{ base }}/api/v1/quantum-scan` is the agent endpoint: `{"domain": "<your-domain>"}` runs the same real scan; `{"key_size": 2048}` alone returns an honest assessment of that RSA key size (no network scan). Any RSA or ECC key size is breakable by Shor's algorithm; key exchange is what needs upgrading.
- Buying the full report ({{ report_price_dual }}): `POST {{ base }}/api/v1/orders` with `{"scan_id": "...", "consent_immediate_delivery": true}` (set the flag only after the payer expressly agreed to immediate delivery and to losing the right of withdrawal) returns a PayPal `approve_url` and a `status_url`. After the payer (or an agent the payer authorized in PayPal) approves, the site captures and verifies the payment automatically, and `GET status_url` returns `report_url`.
- Paying with a direct stablecoin transfer instead: `POST {{ base }}/api/v1/crypto/orders` with `{"scan_id": "...", "network": "polygon-usdt" | "arbitrum-usdc" | "base-usdc", "consent_immediate_delivery": true}` returns a unique `amount` and a `pay_to` address. Send exactly that token amount on the named network, then `POST verify_url` with `{"tx_hash": "0x..."}`; the server checks the transfer on-chain and returns `report_url` once confirmed (HTTP 202 while confirming).
- OpenAPI description: {{ base }}/openapi.yaml

## Grades

- A: TLS 1.3 with hybrid post-quantum key exchange.
- B: TLS 1.3 with classical key exchange only (exposed to harvest-now-decrypt-later).
- C: no TLS 1.3.
- F: invalid certificate, legacy TLS, static RSA key exchange or RSA below 2048 bits.

## Monitoring subscription (for teams)

- {{ base }}/monitoring — daily scans of up to 10 domains ({{ starter_price_dual }}/month) or 100 domains ({{ business_price_dual }}/month), billed monthly through PayPal, cancel any time.
- Free trial: 14 days, up to 10 domains, no payment details; it ends automatically and never turns into a paid subscription by itself. Start at {{ base }}/monitoring#trial (company domain + work email; the dashboard link is emailed).
- Every public IPv4/IPv6 address of a domain (up to 6) gets its own handshake; an alert fires when some addresses negotiate post-quantum key exchange and others do not (CDN edges or load-balanced servers out of sync).
- Email alerts when post-quantum key exchange is lost, a grade changes, a result becomes inconclusive, or a certificate nears expiry.
- Asset discovery: add your base domain (ownership proven by an email on that domain or a DNS TXT record); every hostname with a certificate under it (certificate transparency logs) is looked up weekly, live ones are added to monitoring with a new-asset alert, an alert tells you when hosts exceed your plan, and auto-added hosts that stay unreachable for 7 checks and disappear are removed with the reason in the alert.
- Check history: every daily and manual check is kept for 400 days in the dashboard, with a CSV export (time, grade, key-exchange group, TLS version, certificate days left, addresses post-quantum/total, error, scanner version, measurement note) for security teams and auditors.

## Per-domain pages and comparison

- {{ base }}/site/{domain} — public, indexable page with a domain's latest known grade (from a recent scan or the top-1000 study) and a ready badge snippet.
- {{ base }}/compare?a=<your-domain>&b=<competitor-domain> — scan two sites side by side (replace both placeholders with real hostnames the user asked about).
- CLI: `npx quantum-aether {domain}` (Node ≥18) prints the grade in your terminal; `--json` for machine output.
- GitHub Action: `uses: moncef00327-cloud/pq-tls-action@v1` with `domain:` checks post-quantum TLS on every deploy; optional `require-post-quantum: true` fails the job if X25519MLKEM768 is missing. Marketplace: https://github.com/marketplace/actions/post-quantum-tls-check-quantum-aether
